messages:
alex: Forwarding a customer error — they hit a hard failure when calling a tool. Customer says it worked before.
alex: Paste of the request body they sent:
```json
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-1\",
  \"input\": \"start job\",
  \"tool_call\": {
    \"name\": \"run_shell\",
    \"args\": \"{\\\"cmd\\\": \\\"C:\\\\\\\\Program Files\\\\\\\\app\\\\\\\\run.exe\\\",}\"\"\n  }
}
```
alex: They also included request id `req_01GxY...` and region `us-west-2`.
ingrid: can you paste the API response and headers? which SDK/version are they using?
alex: response body:
```json
{ \"error\": \"tool_call.invalid_args\", \"message\": \"Failed to parse tool args: trailing comma at position 64\", \"status\": 400 }
```
alex: headers: `x-request-id: req_01GxY...`, `x-client-version: js-2.4.1`
devx-bot: quick lint: looks like unescaped backslashes + a trailing comma inside the stringified args. Happens when clients stringify the args object and then embed that string into JSON without escaping or they accidentally leave a trailing comma. :face_with_monocle:
maria: I reproduced locally using a curl payload that mirrors the customer's body and got the same parse error. Repro (shell quoting intentionally messy to show the root cause):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1\",\"tool_call\":{\"name\":\"run_shell\",\"args\":\"{\"cmd\":\"C:\\\\\\\\Program Files\\\\\\\\app\\\\\\\\run.exe\",}\"}}'
```
maria: you can see the inner JSON used for `args` is not properly escaped for the shell and it also has a trailing comma after the path. That produces an invalid JSON string to the runtime.
ingrid: short-term guidance for customer: send `args` as a JSON object (recommended), not a string, or ensure any JSON-encoded string is fully escaped and has no trailing commas. Example correct body (object-form):
```json
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-1\",
  \"tool_call\": {
    \"name\": \"run_shell\",
    \"args\": { \"cmd\": \"C:\\\\Program Files\\\\app\\\\run.exe\" }
  }
}
```
ingrid: if they must pass `args` as a string (legacy clients), escaped-string example: `\"args\": \"{\\\"cmd\\\": \\\"C:\\\\\\\\Program Files\\\\\\\\app\\\\\\\\run.exe\\\"}\"` — note the double-escaping.
alex: customer says their in-house serializer changed recently and introduced a trailing comma. They've rolled back and that fixes it, but they asked whether Redwood could be more lenient and accept trailing commas/extra whitespace to reduce breakage.
maria: security/parse policy note — runtime deliberately uses strict JSON parsing for tool args to avoid ambiguous edge cases and potential injection into tool payloads. Accepting lenient JSON increases risk surface. Eng-runtime should evaluate with security.
alex: customer also requested a preflight diagnostic endpoint or client-side validator to check tool args before send.
ingrid: action items: 
- alex -> send repro payload + `x-request-id` to eng-runtime and include exact logs (I will attach router logs).
- maria -> draft JS/python snippets showing correct serialization patterns and common pitfalls (double stringifying, shell quoting).
- sre-oncall -> run quick query to count similar failures in last 30d and surface spikes (:hourglass:).
sre-oncall: I'll add a short-term alert and check error-rate for `tool_call.invalid_args`.
alex: I'll reply to customer with rollback workaround + recommended payload examples and say we escalated for product discussion. :white_check_mark:
